html:
The arrival of the dingo, a lineage of dog, in Australia about 3,500 years ago.

The dingo must have come by boat, most likely with seafarers from island Southeast Asia, though no one knows who brought it. It never reached Tasmania, which had been cut off from the mainland by rising seas thousands of years earlier. On the mainland the dingo became the top land predator. Around the same time the thylacine and the Tasmanian devil died out on the mainland but survived in Tasmania, and many scientists think the dingo was part of the reason.

Many Aboriginal peoples took dingo pups from the wild and raised them as companions, hunting partners and bed warmers on cold nights. Dingoes appear in rock art and in many Dreaming stories. After British settlement they were treated as pests that killed sheep, and the Dingo Fence was built across the southeast to keep them out of grazing land. Compare the much later spread of merino sheep and rabbits.
sum: The arrival of the dingo, a lineage of dog, in Australia about 3,500 years ago.
